title: Most People Expect AI to Reduce Jobs for Humans
paragraphs: Artificial intelligence is changing the way many people work. However, according to a large new survey by the Pew Research Center, people around the world are more likely to expect AI to reduce the number of jobs than to create new ones.
The survey asked 42,151 people in 37 countries and territories about their views on AI. It was carried out between February and May 2026, and the results were published in September.

In 34 of the 37 places surveyed, people were more likely to say that AI would lead to fewer jobs over the next 20 years than to say it would lead to more jobs. Across all the countries, a median of 46% of people expected AI to reduce jobs, while only 9% expected it to create them.

Concern was particularly high in wealthy countries. In Australia and South Korea, 76% of adults expected AI to lead to fewer jobs, and in the United States, the figure was 71%. In the US, this was 7 percentage points higher than two years earlier. In contrast, only 26% of people in Nigeria and the Philippines expected job losses. However, in many middle-income countries, large numbers of people said they were unsure.

The survey also found differences between groups of people. In several countries, young adults aged 18 to 34 were more worried about job losses than people aged 50 and older. In 11 mostly wealthy countries, women were more likely than men to expect job losses.
People were also worried about inequality. In general, more people believed that AI would increase the gap between rich and poor than believed it would reduce it.

Despite these concerns, many people had mixed feelings about AI. Across the countries, a median of 41% said they were equally concerned and excited about AI, while 37% said they were more concerned than excited. Israel was the only country where more people were mainly excited than mainly concerned.
It is important to remember that the survey measured people's expectations, not actual job losses.
